evidence: Cic. Att. 3.24.2: tōta rēs quō locō sit
Liv. 2.47.5: quō locō rēs essent (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Latin speaks of the matter itself: quō locō rēs est?, how do things stand?; quae cum ita sint, this being the situation.

evidence: Verg. A. 2.322: quō rēs summa locō? (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: in aliquō locō esse, to be in a certain position or state.

evidence: Cic. Fam. 1.8.1: dē tōtō statū rērum commūnium
terms.comment: The state of things as a whole, especially public affairs.

evidence: Cic. Planc. 11: est haec condiciō līberōrum populōrum (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of the position someone is placed in.

phrases.latin: haec rēs quem ad modum ceciderit et tōta rēs quō locō sit velim ad mē scrībās
phrases.english: please write and tell me how this business turned out and how the whole situation stands

phrases.latin: Tū sī hīc sīs, aliter sentiās.
phrases.english: If you were in my position, you would feel differently.

phrases.latin: dē tōtō statū rērum commūnium cognōscēs
phrases.english: you will learn about the whole state of public affairs

sources: Lewis & Short: res · Lewis & Short: locus · Lewis & Short: status · Lewis & Short: condicio
